summary: Skills collection bundling third-party scripts; no installer-side attack behavior observed
details: Package bundles a collection of 'skills' consisting of helper scripts for various tools (web scrapers, benchmarks, rclone CLI installer, YouTube note-taker verification). Static pattern matches fire on routine primitives in these bundled scripts: Python scrapers that issue HTTP GET/POST requests (base_scraper.py, serve_api.py), a benchmark runner shell script, an rclone installer that fetches from rclone.org (the official rclone project domain), and a verify.sh that uses curl for GET requests. The matched tokens (ping/curl/GET/POST/install) co-occur as expected for scraper and installer tooling and are not wired to credential reads, environment scraping, or exfiltration to attacker-controlled destinations. The rclone install script fetches from the tool's official domain, which is standard practice for that ecosystem. No lifecycle hook executes these scripts on npm install; they are data/assets of the skills bundle that run only when a user explicitly invokes them.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
